MOD_WF_CONFLICT_TITLE: Worker Folks: Hiring is switched off
MOD_WF_CONFLICT_TEXT:
The mod ${mod} is loaded, and the two mods change the same mechanic: which skill the game treats as active and what keeps running when you start another one. ${mod} lets your character run every skill at once; Worker Folks lets hired Folks hold skills beside your own action. Loaded together they would fight over the active action and break skill timers, so Worker Folks has disabled itself for this session.

To use Worker Folks, disable ${mod} in the Mod Manager and reload. Nothing in your save was changed.

MOD_WF_TIP_9: Settling costs the owed wages plus a severance of 5% of your next hire’s price. Then the Folk cools down. Pay three times the severance to skip the cooldown.
MOD_WF_TIP_10: Folks work offline like your own action. The Welcome Back window lists what each Folk did and who went into debt or on strike.

MOD_WF_SETTING_QUALIFICATION_HINT:
A Folk works a skill only once your own level in it is 10 for a Trainee, 30 for an Apprentice, 50 for a Journeyman, 70 for a Master and 90 for a Foreman; from the Folk's mastery 50 the level of the tier below is enough.
Off: Folks work any skill.
MOD_WF_SETTING_FAST_MASTERY_HINT:
Mastery bars and mastery pool bars are updated without searching the whole page on every mastery gain, and the GP shown after a wage and the Completion Log's progress are redrawn at most a few times a second, which made the game stutter whenever an action finished, more so with many Folks.
Off: the game's own way, in case a bar or an amount from another mod stops updating.

MOD_WF_ORDERS_HELP_1: Only items your Folks make count, from the moment an order appears. What you make yourself doesn’t, and neither does anything made before. An item counts when it reaches your bank, so selling or using it later changes nothing.
MOD_WF_ORDERS_HELP_2: A share of the wages its own work cost you, rolled from ×0.5 to ×3 when the order appears; with wages off it pays no GP. Hiring XP: a tenth of a level’s worth for a Small order, a fifth for a Medium, two fifths for a Large, at your level when it’s delivered. A Medium order adds a Hiring mastery token. A Large one adds the extra its card shows: tokens, a diploma, junk or gems.
MOD_WF_ORDERS_HELP_3: Every 24 hours of game time, offline included, the board refreshes. Delivered orders and ones nobody started go. An order in progress gets one more day, then it goes undelivered. A delivered order’s place stays empty until the refresh. Your Hiring level opens more: 2 Small orders at 8, 3 with Medium ones at 30, a reroll for 1M GP at 50, 4 with Large ones at 70.

MOD_WF_DREAM_021: ${name} could really go for a bowl of soup right now.
MOD_WF_DREAM_022: ${name} was handed lemons once. Made lemonade. Feels wise.
MOD_WF_DREAM_023: ${name} sniffs the air. Somewhere, someone is baking bread.
MOD_WF_DREAM_024: ${name} has opinions about cheese. Strong ones.
MOD_WF_DREAM_025: ${name} pictures being a famous chef. With a very tall hat.
MOD_WF_DREAM_026: ${name} wonders when its birthday is. Nobody wrote it down.
MOD_WF_DREAM_027: ${name} hums a little song about copper and tin.
MOD_WF_DREAM_028: ${name} can’t decide if coal is a rock or a mood.
MOD_WF_DREAM_029: ${name} found gold once. It was a shiny pebble.
MOD_WF_DREAM_030: ${name} wonders if dragonite ore comes from dragons.
MOD_WF_DREAM_031: ${name} daydreams about a diamond the size of a fist.
MOD_WF_DREAM_032: ${name} hears a pickaxe in the distance and smiles.
MOD_WF_DREAM_033: ${name} admires a runite bar. So blue. So heavy.
MOD_WF_DREAM_034: ${name} pictures a bronze sword and a heroic pose.
MOD_WF_DREAM_035: ${name} tries on a dragon platebody in its head. Fits great.
MOD_WF_DREAM_036: Clang, clang, clang. ${name} finds it oddly relaxing.
MOD_WF_DREAM_037: ${name} named the potatoes. That was a mistake at dinner.
MOD_WF_DREAM_038: ${name} dreams of the first slice of a cold watermelon.
MOD_WF_DREAM_039: ${name} thinks compost is underrated. Nobody asked.
MOD_WF_DREAM_040: ${name} plants a magic seed in its mind. It grows sideways.
MOD_WF_DREAM_041: ${name} wonders if the crops miss it while it’s away.
MOD_WF_DREAM_042: ${name} still has nightmares about cabbage week.
MOD_WF_DREAM_043: ${name} misses the crackle of a campfire at night.
MOD_WF_DREAM_044: ${name} watches ash float away and thinks big thoughts.
MOD_WF_DREAM_045: ${name} wonders what’s in every pocket it walks past.
MOD_WF_DREAM_046: ${name} pictures a coin purse that fills itself.
MOD_WF_DREAM_047: ${name} imagines a disguise so good even golbins wave.
MOD_WF_DREAM_048: ${name} counts feathers. Loses count. Starts over.
MOD_WF_DREAM_049: ${name} dreams of hitting the target. Any target.
MOD_WF_DREAM_050: ${name} once hit a bullseye. The target was very close.
MOD_WF_DREAM_051: ${name}’s feet hurt. It dreams of soft leather boots.
MOD_WF_DREAM_052: ${name} would like a ring. Just to fidget with.
MOD_WF_DREAM_053: ${name} plans to knit a scarf. It has never knitted.
MOD_WF_DREAM_054: ${name} wonders what an air rune weighs. Probably nothing.
MOD_WF_DREAM_055: ${name} keeps a fire rune for cold nights. In theory.
MOD_WF_DREAM_056: ${name} waves a hand. Nothing happens. Worth a try.
MOD_WF_DREAM_057: ${name} dreams of a wand that does the chores.
MOD_WF_DREAM_058: ${name} pictures itself in a pointy hat. Looks very wise.
MOD_WF_DREAM_059: ${name} sniffs a herb and pretends to know what it does.
MOD_WF_DREAM_060: ${name} wonders what a perfect swing feels like.
MOD_WF_DREAM_061: ${name} pictures leaping a log gracefully. Lands on it.
MOD_WF_DREAM_062: ${name} would summon a helper. For its own chores.
MOD_WF_DREAM_063: ${name} counts stars and finds one shaped like a pickaxe.
MOD_WF_DREAM_064: ${name} keeps a pinch of stardust for luck. It’s mostly dust.
MOD_WF_DREAM_065: ${name} dreams of a little house with a little garden.
MOD_WF_DREAM_066: ${name} says a small prayer for shorter shifts.
MOD_WF_DREAM_067: ${name} is glad it was hired for skills, not monsters.
MOD_WF_DREAM_068: ${name} practises a fierce face in a puddle.
MOD_WF_DREAM_069: ${name} dreams of armour that also keeps the rain off.
MOD_WF_DREAM_070: ${name} feels fine. Mostly. A nap would help.
MOD_WF_DREAM_071: ${name} lifted a full crate once. Mentions it often.
MOD_WF_DREAM_072: ${name} dreams of chickens. They are plotting something.
MOD_WF_DREAM_073: ${name} wonders what cows think about all day.
MOD_WF_DREAM_074: ${name} thinks golbins just need a hug. From far away.
MOD_WF_DREAM_075: ${name} imagines asking a dragon for a light.
MOD_WF_DREAM_076: ${name} checks its boots for spiders. Twice.
MOD_WF_DREAM_077: ${name} heard a ghost last night. It was the wind. Probably.
MOD_WF_DREAM_078: ${name} hopes the Kraken stays in the sea. All of it.
MOD_WF_DREAM_079: ${name} lost a sandwich to a seagull once. Never forgave it.
MOD_WF_DREAM_081: ${name} wonders if wizards get paid by the hour too.
MOD_WF_DREAM_082: ${name} talks to plants. One talked back. Once.
MOD_WF_DREAM_083: ${name} waves at a farmer. The farmer waves a pitchfork back.
MOD_WF_DREAM_084: ${name} hides its wages in a sock. Just in case.
MOD_WF_DREAM_085: ${name} dreams of a duck made of pudding. It wobbles.
MOD_WF_DREAM_086: ${name} wants a pet rock. A cool one.
MOD_WF_DREAM_087: ${name} wonders who is feeding the cat.
MOD_WF_DREAM_089: ${name} feels a bit lonely today. Like a certain lizard.
MOD_WF_DREAM_090: ${name} imagines a chick following it around all day.
MOD_WF_DREAM_091: ${name} wonders how a giraffe would fit in a bank.
MOD_WF_DREAM_092: ${name} dreams of a golden golbin. It’s still a golbin.
MOD_WF_DREAM_093: ${name} pictures a chest full of gold. And snacks.
MOD_WF_DREAM_094: ${name} found a rusty key. Now it needs a door.
MOD_WF_DREAM_095: ${name} wants a party. The hat is ready.
MOD_WF_DREAM_096: ${name} pictures itself in cool glasses. Very cool.
MOD_WF_DREAM_097: ${name} has been good this year. Mostly.
MOD_WF_DREAM_098: ${name} hid an egg somewhere. Forgot where.
MOD_WF_DREAM_099: ${name} wonders what to keep in an empty bottle. Maybe a cloud.
MOD_WF_DREAM_100: ${name} wonders who Bob is and why he left his rake.
MOD_WF_CARD_HAUL_FULL_WHY: Collect its haul to start it again
MOD_WF_HAUL_FULL_NOTICE: Haul full: ${name} stopped. Collect what it holds to start it again; its wages keep running.
MOD_WF_ROOM_TIP_HAUL: Haul, kept until you collect it:
MOD_WF_OWN_STOCK_AWAY: Away from a bank it always works from its own stock.
MOD_WF_AUTO_RESTOCK_OFF: Refills its stock from your bank on its own
MOD_WF_AUTO_RESTOCK_AWAY: Waits for a bank: away it lives on its room
MOD_WF_AUTO_RESTOCK_TIP: When its stock falls below the time you pick, it refills from your bank on its own. A Folk you stopped waits for you.
MOD_WF_OFFLINE_HAUL: ${name} holds ${items} in its haul, waiting for you
MOD_WF_COMM_LOCKED: Opens at Hiring ${level}: the people of your town ask your Folks for their work, and pay in Township resources and Town Standing.
MOD_WF_COMM_LOCKED_TOWN: Found your town in Township first: its people will then bring their requests to your guild.
MOD_WF_COMM_SLOT_LOCKED: Opens at Trusted (${points} / ${need} Standing): a fourth person of your town brings a request.
MOD_WF_COMM_EMPTY: No one is asking. The board fills again at the next refresh.
MOD_WF_COMM_HOURS_TIP: ${skill} · about ${hours} h of work for one Folk
MOD_WF_COMM_FOLK_RUN: ${name} is on the way, back in ${time}
MOD_WF_COMM_RECALL_TIP: Takes the Folk off this commission. What it delivered still counts; what its room holds for the town goes to your bank.
MOD_WF_COMM_SEND_TIP: ${name} works for the ${figure}: what it makes of this item goes to its room. When the room holds the rest, or has no space for one more action, it carries it to town: 45 min of game time without work, paid as wages.
MOD_WF_COMM_RUN_DONE: ${name} delivered ${qty} to the ${figure}; ${left} still to go.
MOD_WF_COMM_CARD_RUN: On the way to the ${figure} · back in ${time}
MOD_WF_COMM_CARD_TIP: The ${figure}’s commission. Only this item counts. It waits in the room until a run carries it to town.
MOD_WF_COMM_LATE: The ${figure}’s ${what} is overdue: deliveries still count, for half the resources.
MOD_WF_COMM_WITHDRAWN: The ${figure} withdrew ${what} and paid ${paid} for what came.
MOD_WF_COMM_STORAGE_FULL: Your town’s storage is full: ${lost} lost.
MOD_WF_COMM_TIER_UP: Your town now counts your guild as ${tier}.
MOD_WF_COMM_HELP_1: A figure of your town asks for an item one of your skills makes: about 8 to 24 hours of work. Send the Folk on that skill. From then on what it makes of that item goes to its room, not your bank. When the room holds the rest, or has no space for one more action, the Folk carries it to town: 45 min of game time without work, paid as wages.
MOD_WF_COMM_HELP_2: Township resources of the figure’s trade: what the town’s own tasks pay at your Township level, ×1.25 for every 8 hours asked, as far as the town’s storage takes them. Town Standing and Hiring XP too. Past the deadline it pays half the resources and less Standing. A day later the figure withdraws and pays only for what came.
MOD_WF_COMM_HELP_3: Three commissions, four from Trusted, one per Folk. Every 24 hours of game time, offline included, delivered and withdrawn ones go and new ones come. At Known (80 Standing) the town gives your guild its charter: build the Guild Hall in Township’s Grasslands: five stages, each -1% Folk wages while kept repaired. Once the Hall stands, your Apprentices and up can find the six Guild Heirlooms as they work; every stage of the Hall and the Square and every story decoration makes a find more likely. At Trusted (300) one hire in four grew up in your town: a Townsfolk, with the Local trait. At Honoured (800) the town grants your guild its Freedom: build the Guild Square in Grasslands: five stages, each +2% happiness and +2% education. Standing fades by 2% a day after three days without a delivery; the charters, the buildings and your Townsfolk stay.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Miller_ASK_1: The wheel housing has rotted through. I need timber before the river rises.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Miller_ASK_2: Winter grinds slow without dry wood for the kiln.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Miller_ASK_3: New beams, new sacks, same old mill. Logs, if your guild can spare them.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Miller_THANKS_1: Good straight grain. The wheel turns again by Sunday.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Miller_THANKS_2: That’s the kiln fed till spring.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Miller_THANKS_3: Stack them by the race. Flour’s on me this week.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Miller_LATE_1: Late, but the mill still stands. Just.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Miller_LATE_2: I’d half given up on you. Half.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Mason_ASK_1: The east wall is more crack than wall. I need good stone, and soon.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Mason_ASK_2: A bridge doesn’t build itself. Bring me what the mine gives.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Mason_ASK_3: The well wants a new lining before the dry months.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Mason_THANKS_1: Solid. You can hear it when you tap it.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Mason_THANKS_2: That’ll hold for a hundred years. Maybe two.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Mason_THANKS_3: Fine work. The wall thanks you, and so do I.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Mason_LATE_1: The scaffold sat empty a week. Still, it’s here.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Mason_LATE_2: The mortar went stiff waiting. Sooner next time.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Smith_ASK_1: The forge is hungry and my racks are bare.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Smith_ASK_2: Every plough in the valley wants mending at once.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Smith_ASK_3: The town guard needs new fittings. I can’t hammer air.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Smith_THANKS_2: The forge sings again. My thanks.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Smith_THANKS_3: Hinges, nails, ploughshares: all from this. Well done.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Smith_LATE_1: The ploughs waited. The fields didn’t.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Baker_ASK_1: Market day is coming and the larder is empty.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Baker_ASK_2: The children ask for more every year. So do their parents.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Baker_ASK_3: The harvest feast needs feeding. Can your guild help?
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Baker_THANKS_1: It smells like a feast already.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Baker_THANKS_3: Fresh and plenty. Bless your cooks.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Baker_LATE_1: The feast was thin, but this will do for the next.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Healer_ASK_1: A fever is going round the lower town. I need remedies.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Healer_ASK_2: My shelves are bare and the winter coughs are coming.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Healer_ASK_3: The guard came back bruised from the road. Potions, please.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Healer_THANKS_1: This will see a few through the night.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Healer_THANKS_2: The fever breaks before this. Thank you.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Healer_THANKS_3: Clear and well brewed. Your Folk knows its herbs.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Healer_LATE_1: Some needed this yesterday. Still, thank you.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Tailor_ASK_1: Cold nights ahead and half the town in thin cloth.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Tailor_ASK_2: Wedding season. Everyone wants something new.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Tailor_ASK_3: The guard’s leathers are more patch than leather.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Tailor_THANKS_1: Fine work. Nobody freezes this year.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Tailor_THANKS_2: The bride will be the talk of the town.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Tailor_THANKS_3: I’ll stitch your guild’s mark in the hem.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Tailor_LATE_1: The cold came first. Now we’re ready for the next.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Fletcher_ASK_1: Archery trials next month, and not a shaft to shoot.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Fletcher_ASK_2: The watchtower’s bows are older than the watchmen.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Fletcher_ASK_3: Hunters are heading north. They’ll want good gear.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Fletcher_THANKS_1: Straight and true. Not a warp among them.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Fletcher_THANKS_2: The trials go ahead. Your guild gets the first shot.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Fletcher_LATE_1: The trials went on without us. Next year, then.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Fletcher_LATE_2: The hunters left light. They’ll be glad of these on their return.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Runewright_ASK_1: The ward-stones are fading. I need runes to renew them.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Runewright_ASK_2: Strange lights over the marsh again. Bring me runes.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Runewright_ASK_3: My apprentices waste more than they make. Help an old runewright.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Runewright_THANKS_1: The wards hum again. The town sleeps safe.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Runewright_THANKS_2: Well bound, well charged. Fine work.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Runewright_THANKS_3: These will hold the marsh lights back a season.
MOD_WF_FIGURE_Runewright_LATE_1: The wards flickered a night or two. No harm, I hope.
MOD_WF_COMM_WITHDRAWN_LOST: The ${figure} withdrew ${what} and paid ${lost} for what came, but your town’s storage is full: all of it was lost.
MOD_WF_COMM_REWARD_LOST_TIP: Your town’s storage was full when this was paid; what found no room was lost. Build storage in Township to keep the next reward.
MOD_WF_COMM_REWARD_ROOM: Your town’s storage has room for ${free} more now: the rest of this reward would be lost.
MOD_WF_COMM_CHARTER_GIVEN_Guild_Charter: Your town counts your guild as Known and hands you its Guild Charter. Build the Guild Hall in Township’s Grasslands: five stages, each -1% Folk wages.
MOD_WF_ITEM_Guild_Charter_DESC: Your town’s word that your guild belongs here, given at Known Town Standing. Township’s Guild Hall asks for it: build it in Grasslands: five stages, each -1% Folk wages.
MOD_WF_COMM_CHARTER_GIVEN_Freedom_of_the: Your town counts your guild as Honoured and grants it the Freedom of the Town. Build the Guild Square in Township’s Grasslands: five stages, each +2% happiness and +2% education.
MOD_WF_ITEM_Freedom_of_the_Town_DESC: Your town’s highest honour, granted to your guild at Honoured Town Standing. Township’s Guild Square asks for it: build it in Grasslands: five stages, each +2% happiness and +2% education.
MOD_WF_COMM_TIER_GIVES_Trusted: A fourth commission comes to the board, and one hire in four now grew up in your town.
MOD_WF_COMM_TOWNSFOLK_HIRED: ${name} grew up in your town: a Townsfolk, with the Local trait.
MOD_WF_STORY_Mill_Bridge_STEP_1: The spring flood took the footbridge to the mill. Timber first, for the piles.
MOD_WF_STORY_Mill_Bridge_STEP_2: The piles are in. Now ore for the ironwork: bolts, straps, a railing that lasts.
MOD_WF_STORY_Mill_Bridge_STEP_3: Smelt it into bars and the smith forges the last of the ironwork.
MOD_WF_STORY_Mill_Bridge_DONE: Carts cross to the mill again, and the bridge already has your guild’s name.
MOD_WF_STORY_Mill_Bridge_HISTORY: The flood took the footbridge to the mill; your guild rebuilt it, timber, ironwork and all.
MOD_WF_STORY_Mill_Bridge_DEED_DESC: Your town’s thanks for the Mill Bridge. Township’s Mill Bridge asks for it: build it once in Grasslands, +1% happiness.
MOD_WF_STORY_Great_Anvil_STEP_1: The town’s great anvil cracked at the horn. Casting a new one takes ore, a lot of it.
MOD_WF_STORY_Great_Anvil_STEP_2: The ore’s in. Smelt it into bars and I pour the anvil this week.
MOD_WF_STORY_Great_Anvil_STEP_3: The anvil rings true. Now make something worthy to be the first work forged on it.
MOD_WF_STORY_Great_Anvil_DONE: The new anvil stands by the forge, its first work hung above the door.
MOD_WF_STORY_Great_Anvil_HISTORY: The town’s great anvil cracked; your guild brought the ore, the bars and the first work forged on the new one.
MOD_WF_STORY_Great_Anvil_DEED_DESC: Your town’s thanks for the Great Anvil. Township’s Great Anvil asks for it: build it once in Grasslands, +1% happiness.
MOD_WF_STORY_Herb_Garden_STEP_1: I want a garden of healing herbs by the infirmary. Potions first, to trade for the seed stock.
MOD_WF_STORY_Herb_Garden_STEP_2: Digging beds is hungry work. Feed the diggers and the beds are done by dusk.
MOD_WF_STORY_Herb_Garden_STEP_3: Last, the trellises, pots and markers: something well made, from your crafters.
MOD_WF_STORY_Herb_Garden_DONE: The garden blooms by the infirmary. Folk come for the smell alone.
MOD_WF_STORY_Herb_Garden_HISTORY: The Healer’s garden of healing herbs, paid for, dug and fitted out by your guild.
MOD_WF_STORY_Herb_Garden_DEED_DESC: Your town’s thanks for the Healer’s Garden. Township’s Healer’s Garden asks for it: build it once in Grasslands, +1% happiness.
MOD_WF_STORY_Winter_Hearth_STEP_1: The cold is in the town’s bones. Warm leather first, for those who sleep rough.
MOD_WF_STORY_Winter_Hearth_STEP_2: A hearth hall needs a pot on the fire: hot food for everyone who comes in.
MOD_WF_STORY_Winter_Hearth_STEP_3: And logs, stacked high, so the fire burns till the thaw.
MOD_WF_STORY_Winter_Hearth_DONE: The fire is lit. No one in town sleeps cold this year.
MOD_WF_STORY_Winter_Hearth_HISTORY: One hard winter your guild clothed, fed and warmed the town at the Winter Hearth.
MOD_WF_STORY_Winter_Hearth_DEED_DESC: Your town’s thanks for the Winter Hearth. Township’s Winter Hearth asks for it: build it once in Grasslands, +1% happiness.
MOD_WF_STORY_Harvest_Pavilion_STEP_1: The harvest feast needs a pavilion and a table to match. Fish first, for the smoking racks.
MOD_WF_STORY_Harvest_Pavilion_STEP_2: Now the cooking: the whole town eats at the feast.
MOD_WF_STORY_Harvest_Pavilion_STEP_3: And runes for the lanterns, so the feast goes on after dark.
MOD_WF_STORY_Harvest_Pavilion_DONE: The feast ran till dawn under the rune lanterns. The pavilion stays up for next year.
MOD_WF_STORY_Harvest_Pavilion_HISTORY: The harvest feast your guild fed and lit; its pavilion still stands by the square.
MOD_WF_STORY_Harvest_Pavilion_DEED_DESC: Your town’s thanks for the Harvest Pavilion. Township’s Harvest Pavilion asks for it: build it once in Grasslands, +1% happiness.
MOD_WF_STORY_RIBBON_TIP: A story: a project of your town in three commissions. Deliver a step and the next takes its place; the last one finishes the story, and the town hands over a deed for a decoration in Township.
MOD_WF_STORY_NEXT: ${story}: step ${step} of ${steps} is on the board.
MOD_WF_STORY_DEED_GIVEN: The town hands your guild the deed for the ${building}. Build it once in Township’s Grasslands: +1% happiness.
MOD_WF_STORY_ENDED: The ${figure} gives up on ${story} for now. It may come back to your board later.
MOD_WF_STORY_HISTORY_NONE: No story told yet. From Honoured, every fifth new commission can be one.
MOD_WF_COMM_HELP_4: From Honoured, every fifth new commission can be a story: a project of your town in three steps, each a commission of its own on a board slot. Deliver a step and the next takes its place. Finish the third and the town hands over a deed: build the story’s decoration once in Township’s Grasslands, +1% happiness and a better chance of Guild Heirlooms. Some stories come only in their season. A withdrawn step ends the story; it can come back later. The book beside your Standing keeps the Town history.
MOD_WF_TRAIT_Local_DESC: Runs to town take half the time; while your town’s happiness is ${need}% or more, the cooldown after a settled strike is halved
MOD_WF_TRAIT_Local_NOW_OFF: Your town’s happiness is ${happiness}% now, under ${need}%
MOD_WF_TRAIT_Local_LASTS: Born in your town: never learned, never forgotten
MOD_WF_TOWNSFOLK_BADGE: Townsfolk: grew up in your town
MOD_WF_COMM_REWARD_ROOM_NONE: Your town’s storage is full now: this reward would be lost. Build storage in Township before it is paid.
MOD_WF_BACKUP_HINT: A code that holds your Folks and everything of this mod: keep it to bring them back if the mod is ever off, uninstalled or fails to load
MOD_WF_BACKUP_ALSO: And each Folk’s gear, room, place and wages, the Payroll Reserve, mastery, Work Orders and Township Commissions, with your settings.
MOD_WF_BACKUP_KEEP: The game forgets your Folks if it ever saves without the mod: turned off, uninstalled or failing to load. Restore, at the foot of this page, brings them back from this code.
MOD_WF_BACKUP_COPY_FAILED: Copying didn’t work here: select the code and copy it by hand.
MOD_WF_BACKUP_DOWNLOAD_FAILED: The download didn’t work here: copy the code instead.
MOD_WF_BACKUP_FAILED: The backup could not be made: reload the game and try again.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_HINT: Bring your Folks back from a backup code
MOD_WF_RESTORE_PASTE: Paste a backup code, or load the file you downloaded.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_LOAD_FAILED: That file could not be read: paste the code instead.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_REPLACES: It replaces your crew and level ${now} with the backup’s, at level ${then}.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_LEAVE: Hired since the backup, they leave: ${names}.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_HANDED_BACK: Gear, room stacks and Reserve your crew holds beyond the backup’s go to your bank.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_KEEPS_BOARDS: Your crew is still here, so Work Orders and Township Commissions stay as they are now: nothing finished since is paid twice.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_TAKEN: Your Folks hold these again, and they reached your bank after the backup, so they come out of it:
MOD_WF_RESTORE_OTHER_MODE: It was made in another game mode: the level caps stay as they are.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_BANK_HEAD: Back to the bank, the shop and Township
MOD_WF_RESTORE_BANK_NONE: Nothing to add: the bank, the shop and Township already hold it all.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_VOYAGE_AFTER: If Voyage needs its backup too, restore it after this one, so it finds your Folks back.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_VOYAGE_OFF: Voyage isn’t loaded now, so these Folks stop walking where they stand: ${names}.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_RELOAD: The game saves and reloads to finish; choose your character again.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_FAILED: The restore could not be finished, and nothing was saved: the game reloads as it was.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_EMPTY: Paste a code or load a file first.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_NOTCODE: That is not a Worker Folks backup code.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_VOYAGE: That is a Voyage backup: restore it from the foot of the Voyage page.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_BROKEN: The code is cut or broken: copy all of it again.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_CHECKSUM: The code was changed somewhere: copy all of it again.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_FORMAT: The code is from another version of these backups.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_NEWER: The code is from a newer version of the mod: update it first.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_RECORD: The save inside the code can’t be read.
MOD_WF_RESTORE_WHY_CANTUNZIP: This browser can’t open a packed code: try it in the Steam game or a current browser.
